pages.quiz:
HOME SCIENCE MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ventilation and Lighting? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Ventilation and Lighting.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ventilation and Lighting.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Yeast Products? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Yeast Products.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Yeast Products.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Yeast Products.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Yeast Products.

3. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Careers in Food and Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Careers in Food and Nutrition.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Convenience Foods? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Convenience Foods.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Convenience Foods.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Convenience Foods.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Convenience Foods.

9. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Heating until a solid melts

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.

11. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

12. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Child Health Care and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Careers in Home Management 3.0 Clothing and Textiles 3.1 Clothing Construction P and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Careers in Home Management and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Clothing Construction Processes: Facings 3.2 Clothing Construction Processes: Co and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting.

2. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Yeast Products.

3. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

4. D — newton (N)

5. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.

7. C — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Convenience Foods.

9. C — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

10. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.

11. B — Glucose and oxygen

12. A — 100 °C

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Child Health Care; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Careers in Home Management 3.0 Clothing and Textiles 3.1 Clothing Construction P; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Careers in Home Management; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Clothing Construction Processes: Facings 3.2 Clothing Construction Processes: Co; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
